newsitem.title: USA: Airport Systems gets Indonesia contract.
newsitem.headline: Airport Systems gets Indonesia contract.

text.p: Airport Systems International Inc said Thursday it received a $17.7 million contract to provide Indonesia with air navigation equipment.
The contract will "have a significant positive impact on our financial performance over the nexxt two years," the company said.
The deal represents a threefold increase in the company's backlog of $6 million and the value is 125 percent of the company's fiscal 1996 sales of $14.2 million, Airport Systems said.
Airport Systems said the contract, which is the largest for the company, is for the delivery of 19 DVORs (Doppler VHF Omni Range equipment) and 22 DMEs (distance measuring equipment).
The contract also provides installation, flight inspection, training and other support services over a two-year period, the company said.
Airport Systems aims to to commence work early in calendar 1997, it said, noting that the program will improve its qualifications for similar future projects.
Airport Systems said that in Indonesia and the Asia/Pacific region alone, it believes the potential for the navigation aid business over the next several years exceeds $200 million.
